examination: Civil Services Mains Examination - Optional Subject
provenance_note: Unit text is the published UPSC syllabus for Anthropology Paper II, corroborated across independent reproductions. NOT diffed against the notification PDF. Verify before promoting any mention to verified.
structure_note: Numbered 1.1/1.2/... with no lettered parts, so section_ref is omitted. UPSC's numbering is preserved at the head of each macro_topic.
paper_title_note: paper_title MUST equal subjects.name for slug upsc-cse-mains-opt-anthropology-p2 exactly.

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 1.1 Evolution of Indian culture and civilization
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 1.1 Evolution of the Indian Culture and Civilization - Prehistoric (Palaeolithic, Mesolithic, Neolithic and Neolithic-Chalcolithic); Protohistoric (Indus Civilization): Pre-Harappan, Harappan and post-Harappan cultures; Contributions of tribal cultures to Indian civilization.
micro_themes: Prehistoric India: Palaeolithic and Mesolithic cultures
Neolithic and Neolithic-Chalcolithic cultures
Protohistoric India: pre-Harappan, Harappan and post-Harappan cultures
Contributions of tribal cultures to Indian civilization

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 1.2-1.3 Palaeo-anthropological evidence and ethno-archaeology in India
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 1.2 Palaeo-anthropological evidences from India with special reference to Siwaliks and Narmada basin (Ramapithecus, Sivapithecus and Narmada Man). 1.3 Ethno-archaeology in India: The concept of ethno-archaeology; Survivals and Parallels among the hunting, foraging, fishing, pastoral and peasant communities including arts and crafts producing communities.
micro_themes: Palaeo-anthropological evidence from the Siwaliks: Ramapithecus and Sivapithecus
Narmada basin and Narmada Man
The concept of ethno-archaeology
Survivals and parallels among hunting, foraging and fishing communities
Survivals and parallels among pastoral, peasant and craft-producing communities

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 2. Demographic profile of India - Ethnic and linguistic elements in the Indian population and their distribution; Indian population - factors influencing its structure and growth.
micro_themes: Ethnic elements in the Indian population and their distribution
Linguistic elements in the Indian population and their distribution
Factors influencing the structure and growth of the Indian population

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 3. The structure and nature of traditional Indian social system - Varnashram, Purushartha, Karma, Rina and Rebirth.
micro_themes: Varnashrama and the traditional social order
Purushartha
Karma, Rina and Rebirth

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 4. Caste system in India: (a) Structure and characteristics - Varna and caste, Theories of origin of caste system, Dominant caste, Caste mobility, Future of caste system, Jajmani system, Tribe-caste continuum. (b) Sacred Complex and Nature-Man-Spirit Complex. (c) Impact of Buddhism, Jainism, Islam and Christianity on Indian society.
micro_themes: Varna and caste; theories of the origin of the caste system
Dominant caste, caste mobility and the future of the caste system
Jajmani system
Tribe-caste continuum
Sacred Complex and Nature-Man-Spirit Complex
Impact of Buddhism and Jainism on Indian society
Impact of Islam and Christianity on Indian society

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 5 Emergence and growth of anthropology in India
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 5. Emergence and growth of anthropology in India - Contributions of the 18th, 19th and early 20th Century scholar-administrators; Contributions of Indian anthropologists to tribal and caste studies.
micro_themes: Contributions of 18th and 19th century scholar-administrators
Contributions of early 20th century scholar-administrators
Contributions of Indian anthropologists to tribal studies
Contributions of Indian anthropologists to caste studies

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 6. Indian Village - Significance of village study in India; Indian village as a social system; Traditional and changing patterns of settlement and inter-caste relations; Agrarian relations in Indian villages; Impact of globalization on Indian villages.
micro_themes: Significance of village study in India
The Indian village as a social system
Traditional and changing patterns of settlement and inter-caste relations
Agrarian relations in Indian villages
Impact of globalization on Indian villages

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 7. Linguistic and religious minorities and their social, political and economic status.
micro_themes: Linguistic minorities and their social, political and economic status
Religious minorities and their social, political and economic status

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 8. Indigenous and exogenous processes of socio-cultural change in Indian society: Sanskritization, Westernization, Modernization; Inter-play of little and great traditions; Panchayati raj and social change; Media and social change.
micro_themes: Sanskritization
Westernization and Modernization
Interplay of little and great traditions
Panchayati Raj and social change
Media and social change

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 9.1 Tribal situation in India - Bio-genetic variability, linguistic and socio-economic characteristics of tribal populations and their distribution. 9.2 Problems of the tribal communities - land alienation, poverty, indebtedness, low literacy, poor educational facilities, unemployment, underemployment, health and nutrition. 9.3 Developmental projects and their impact on tribal displacement and problems of rehabilitation; Development of forest policy and tribals; Impact of urbanization and industrialization on tribal populations.
micro_themes: Bio-genetic variability of tribal populations
Linguistic and socio-economic characteristics of tribal populations and their distribution
Land alienation, poverty and indebtedness among tribal communities
Low literacy, poor educational facilities, unemployment and underemployment
Health and nutrition among tribal communities
Developmental projects, tribal displacement and rehabilitation
Development of forest policy and tribals
Impact of urbanization and industrialization on tribal populations

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 10 Exploitation, deprivation and contemporary tribal society
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 10.1 Problems of exploitation and deprivation of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes; Constitutional safeguards for Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes. 10.2 Social change and contemporary tribal societies: Impact of modern democratic institutions, development programmes and welfare measures on tribals and weaker sections. 10.3 The concept of ethnicity; Ethnic conflicts and political developments; Unrest among tribal communities; Regionalism and demand for autonomy; Pseudo-tribalism; Social change among the tribes during colonial and post-Independent India.
micro_themes: Exploitation and deprivation of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and OBCs
Constitutional safeguards for Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes
Impact of modern democratic institutions on tribals and weaker sections
Impact of development programmes and welfare measures
The concept of ethnicity; ethnic conflicts and political developments
Unrest among tribal communities; regionalism and demand for autonomy
Pseudo-tribalism
Social change among tribes during colonial and post-Independent India

syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 11.1 Impact of Hinduism, Buddhism, Christianity, Islam and other religions on tribal societies. 11.2 Tribe and nation state - a comparative study of tribal communities in India and other countries.
micro_themes: Impact of Hinduism and Buddhism on tribal societies
Impact of Christianity, Islam and other religions on tribal societies
Tribe and nation state: comparative study of tribal communities in India and abroad

syllabus_nodes.macro_topic: 12 Tribal administration and the role of anthropology
syllabus_nodes.official_syllabus_line: 12.1 History of administration of tribal areas, tribal policies, plans, programmes of tribal development and their implementation; The concept of PTGs (Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups), their distribution, special programmes for their development; Role of NGOs in tribal development. 12.2 Role of anthropology in tribal and rural development. 12.3 Contributions of anthropology to the understanding of regionalism, communalism, and ethnic and political movements.
micro_themes: History of the administration of tribal areas and tribal policies
Plans and programmes of tribal development and their implementation
Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups: distribution and special programmes
Role of NGOs in tribal development
Role of anthropology in tribal and rural development
Contribution of anthropology to understanding regionalism and communalism
Contribution of anthropology to understanding ethnic and political movements
